newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss short money steady, forecast startles.
newsitem.headline: Swiss short money steady, forecast startles.

text.p: Swiss money rates were largely steady in early trade, with tomorrow/next money quoted at 1-3/8 percent to 1-1/2 percent as attention focused on an interest rate forecast published by Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB).
The report forecast sharp drops in Swiss short-term rates over six months.
The report may have led to stop-loss orders in EuroSwiss futures, but the expectations for sharply lower Swiss rates were not shared by most traders.
"It is a singular opinion," said one trader at another bank.
Traders also said they did not expect the Swiss National Bank (SNB) to lower interest rates at its regular weekly meeting today. The discount rate is now at 1.00 percent.
The SNB is expected to give results of the meeting by 1200 GMT.
The CSFB report forecast three-month Swiss money rates at a midrate of 0.50 percent six months hence.
Currently three-month rates are at roughly 1-3/4 percent to 2.00 percent.
It also forecast a mark/Swiss rate much higher than currently, at 93.00 centimes.
This would imply that the mark would strengthen from present levels just over 85.00 centimes.
A trader at a second bank noted that CSFB has forecast much lower interest rates in Switzerland, and that the latest report seemed to go in the same direction.
"That is not the first time that they have given this opinion. They have been very aggressive," the trader said.

According to CSFB, the SNB has shifted somewhat in its stance to give more weight to short term rates, and away from targeting bank reserves. Reserves in the form of sight deposits, together with notes in circulation, comprise the SNB's M0 money aggregate.
The SNB said on Wednesday that growth in the aggregate continued to overshoot its five-year growth target in the first quarter of 1997.
But analysts noted that the aggregate undershot the target in the first year and one-half of the current five-year period which began in 1995.
CSFB analyst Michael Bernegger said he stood behind the forecasts of the bank, but also said the forecasts which the bank published in its report on Wednesday were those which it has had for a while.
